items.title: Nasdaq jumps 2% to close at a record, buoyed by surge in AI stocks, as well as cooling oil and yields
items.content: Nasdaq Composite posts its first record close since June as AI-linked chipmakers regain footing. Oil prices and Treasury yields cooled simultaneously, easing pressure on growth valuations. Breadth improved with semis leading. (Nasdaq ~2% gain; S&P 500 near record territory.)

items.title: US500 rose to 7651 points on September 18, up 0.17% session-on-session
items.content: US benchmark index at 7651, up 0.17% for the session but down 0.75% for the past month, still +14.8% year-on-year. Index consolidating near record highs after the AI-led rebound.

items.title: Hang Seng Index closed at 24,750.78, +0.15% (+36.98 pts)
items.content: Hong Kong benchmark ended the Sept 18 session at 24,750.78, up 36.98 points or 0.15%. Index remains range-bound below the 25,000 psychological level.

items.title: Hang Seng tests 25,050 resistance at cloud top; stuck below 24,981 in no-trade zone
items.content: Technical read: HSI pressing the 25,050 cloud-top resistance while trapped below 24,981 support-turned-resistance. A clean break of 25,050 opens upside; failure keeps the index range-bound.

items.title: China stocks mixed, Hong Kong shares edge higher as AI weakness weighs
items.content: Mainland stocks traded mixed as AI and semiconductor shares fell — CSI AI Index -1.2%, STAR50 -0.9% — while banking stocks rose on defensive rotation. Investors cautious ahead of key global data. (Also reported by Business Recorder, Sep 15.)

items.title: US, Iran engaged in tanker war: where is the months-long conflict headed?
items.content: Washington targeted three Iranian oil tankers while Tehran hit tankers and fired a ballistic missile toward US warships patrolling near the Strait of Hormuz. Escalation in the Persian Gulf shipping lanes directly threatens global oil transit.

items.title: 2026 Iran war — operational standoff after fierce July combat, Hormuz shipping lanes being cleared
items.content: Conflict entered a brief operational standoff in August 2026 after fierce July combat, marked by a sharp decline in direct kinetic engagements and an end to Iranian drone attacks on Gulf Arab states. US forces working to clear crucial shipping lanes in the Strait of Hormuz. Tensions stem from failed Geneva nuclear talks.

items.title: 2026 Iran war: despite June MoU to reopen Strait of Hormuz, Iran seeks control and transit fees
items.content: Despite the June 2026 memorandum of understanding aimed at reopening the Strait of Hormuz and ending the war, Iran sought to assert hegemonic control over the strait and eventually collect fees on ships passing through — keeping risk premium in energy markets elevated.

items.title: Strait of Hormuz: security developments and impacts on oil, gas and commodities
items.content: US and Iran agreed a ceasefire in April 2026 and signed a June 2026 MoU, but conflict resumed in July 2026 as Iranian forces attacked commercial shipping deemed noncompliant. CRS flags ongoing risk to oil, gas and commodity flows through the strait.

items.title: Geopolitical risk is the new normal — Asia input shortages from Strait disruption
items.content: Asia faces shortages in fertilizer (food supply), chemicals (tech hardware production) and plastics (autos, pharma), sparking double-digit price increases for these inputs within weeks. Even a rapid reopening of the Strait could leave an 'air pocket' as supply chains normalize slowly.

items.title: Geopolitical Risk Dashboard: fragmentation accelerating on Middle East conflict and US-China tech competition
items.content: Geopolitical fragmentation is accelerating as conflict in the Middle East, US-China technology competition and trade tensions expose vulnerabilities in the global economy. Governments and companies prioritise security, resilience and sovereignty.

items.title: Earnings calendar week of Sept 21–25: 11 reports Tue, 11 Wed, 18 Thu; light Friday
items.content: No market-moving mega-cap results this week; 18 earnings on Thursday Sept 24 peaks the schedule, Friday Sept 25 essentially empty. Focus shifts to macro data (PCE, GDP) rather than single-name earnings.
